clue.text: Shield nurse carrying a head covering backwards

indicators.note: the nurse word carries the next letters held inside it

parts.note: to nurse is to care for someone

indicators.note: backwards means the head covering word is read from right to left

parts.note: a cap is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A nurse wearing her cap the wrong way round while protecting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' is a verb here, to care for, not the person in the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard protective shell on the back of a tortoise or crab, a natural shield.

clue.text: Male (and half male) shellfish

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: half of the word male is taken, here its second two letters

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a shellfish as wholly male plus half male again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' gives a male bird; 'half' takes the second half of the word 'male' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockle is an edible bivalve mollusc, a kind of shellfish sold at seaside stalls.

clue.text: Thoroughly searched, charged and then let go

parts.note: to charge is to run headlong, so charged gives ran
an employee let go has been sacked

explanation.surface: A police raid: a place searched, someone charged and then released.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly, usually leaving disorder behind.

clue.text: Outside church, cut and dried

indicators.note: the cut word sits outside the church abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: pared means trimmed or cut

explanation.surface: Something outside a church described as cut and dried, as in settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut and dried' looks like the idiom for settled, but 'cut' is wordplay and 'dried' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched land or lips have been dried out completely by heat.

clue.text: Provide food for domestic pet (queen)

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Feeding a pet cat, with a nod to a queen being a female cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat, which makes the bracket seem a mere aside about the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply meals or refreshments, for example at a party.

clue.text: Grim and unhappy maids facing student

indicators.note: unhappy suggests the letters of maids are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Miserable maids standing in front of a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' looks like part of the definition but signals the anagram of MAIDS, giving DISMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and grim are synonyms, both meaning gloomy and depressing.

clue.text: UN tried desperately to enter uninvited

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild flailing, so the letters of UN tried are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The United Nations trying hard to get into somewhere it was not asked.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to go in where one is not welcome, an unwanted entry.

clue.text: Thelma or Ian sheltering a New Zealander

indicators.note: the words Thelma or Ian shelter the letters within them, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Two people, Thelma or Ian, giving refuge to a visitor from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian indigenous people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Ship concealing most of gun, I hear

indicators.note: the ship word conceals the shortened gun inside it

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the gun word is dropped

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A ship hiding a weapon, reported by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a link signalling a sound-alike, but it is the definition: what a listener might say of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: One who hears is a listener, so the phrase is that person speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Grace ill, badly suffering from a reaction

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of Grace ill are put together wrongly, into a new order

explanation.surface: Grace is ill, badly affected by something she reacted to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allergic has an immune reaction, such as hay fever, to a substance.

clue.text: Cola nut roasting, cooked and well done

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of cola nut roasting have been tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step: a cola nut being roasted, then cooked thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well done' looks like a cooking instruction, but it is the definition: praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying well done to someone is offering them praise for an achievement.

clue.text: Tanned skin — it's ecstasy in soapy water

indicators.note: in places the ecstasy letter within the soapy water word

parts.note: lather is the foam made by soap and water
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sunbather's skin enjoying a bath full of suds.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal hide that has been tanned becomes leather, used for shoes and bags.

clue.text: Learned English: ill-mannered about it

indicators.note: about means the rude word goes around the next word

parts.note: rude means ill-mannered

explanation.surface: An English person who is clever but rude about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, said in two syllables, means scholarly and full of knowledge.

clue.text: Driving dangerously in Sierra? Only joking!

parts.note: Sierra is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for S
saying only joking is the same as saying just kidding

explanation.surface: Someone claims to drive dangerously in their Ford Sierra, then laughs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra is also a Ford car, which suits the driving picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A car skidding is sliding out of control, a dangerous way to be driving.

clue.text: Ducks cook gently when lid's removed, son sees occasionally

indicators.note: the lid of a word is its first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently just below the boil

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some of the letters of sees, every other one

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions about cooking ducks, with a son watching now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like the birds being cooked, but it is a verb: dips under water. 'occasionally' takes ES from 'sees'.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, which is to submerge them.

clue.text: Cheer with echo delayed

parts.note: Echo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for E
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A cheer whose echo comes back a moment later.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to elate them, filling them with joy.

clue.text: Stargazing device from earl's boat rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of earl's boat are taken apart and assembled differently

explanation.surface: A nobleman's boat dismantled and turned into an instrument for the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The astrolabe was an old instrument for measuring the positions of stars and planets.

clue.text: Old clothes: a couple of shirts perhaps?

parts.note: a couple of something is a double quantity
a T is a T-shirt, so two of them in the plural are Ts

explanation.surface: Old garments described as a mere pair of shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that T-shirts are only one kind of shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Doublets were the close-fitting padded jackets worn by men in Tudor and Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Demand gold, returning flushed

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: returning means the flushed word is read backwards

parts.note: a flushed face is red

explanation.surface: Someone demanding gold and coming back red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: To order something is to command or demand it.

clue.text: Regret having base metal in train

indicators.note: having means the regret word holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: Regretting carrying cheap metal on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base metal' reads as one phrase but splits: 'base' is E, the base of natural logarithms, and 'metal' is TIN. 'train' is the procession following a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants accompanying an important person, their train.

clue.text: Spice price is steep

parts.note: mace is a spice made from the outer covering of nutmeg
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A complaint that the cost of a spice is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for the price, but it is a verb: to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate food is to soften it by soaking it in liquid, just as one steeps it.

clue.text: Change design and sit once more

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A designer reworking a plan while the model poses again.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order, sit then once more, is reversed in the answer, as in the phrase 'model again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel is to alter the shape or structure of something.

clue.text: If you lose this, you won't know what's going on

definitions.text: If you lose this, you won't know what's going on

parts.words: If you lose this, you won't know what's going on
parts.note: losing the ... of a conversation or story means no longer following it

explanation.surface: A warning about something easily lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of losing the thread describes losing track of an argument or plot.

clue.text: Fish left in hat?

indicators.note: in places the left letter within the hat word

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat

explanation.surface: A fish left inside someone's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring cured by salting and light smoking, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Not in right end of queue? That's weird!

parts.note: not in means out

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of queue

explanation.surface: Someone not standing in the queue, at the right-hand end, which seems odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre, borrowed from French, means unconventional and bizarre.

clue.text: Gigantic flying creature captures a minute male

indicators.note: captures means the flying creature holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a moth is a flying insect

explanation.surface: A huge flying beast catching a tiny man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like tiny, contrasting with gigantic, but it is the time unit M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, from the size of the extinct woolly elephant.

clue.text: A weaving machine set up to make money

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a loom is a machine for weaving cloth

explanation.surface: Installing a loom as a way to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is slang for money or cash.

clue.text: To get this protocol, rearrange a nine-letter code

indicators.note: rearrange tells the solver to put the letters of a nine-letter code into a different order

explanation.surface: Instructions for agreeing a protocol by reworking a coded message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nine-letter' is part of the fodder, not a length hint; the answer is fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French agreement, a diplomatic understanding.

clue.text: Cooked and pickled?

definitions.meaning: simmered slowly in liquid, as with a casserole
pickled is slang for drunk, and so is the answer

explanation.surface: Food cooked, or preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is both a slow-cooking method and British slang for being drunk.

clue.text: This is the end of the line, birdbrain!

definitions.meaning: the terminus of a railway, where the track stops
read cryptically: a rail is a bird and a head holds the brain, so bird plus brain

explanation.surface: A railway terminus, or an insult to a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A railhead is the point where a railway line terminates; the second reading splits it as bird and brain.
